title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base ring with a PD ideal S^+ = (S^+, γ) and a fixed element t ∈ S^+. The page belongs to the construction of a simplicial divided-power de Rham algebra n ↦ A_n^*. Here A_n^* is the PD polynomial de Rham complex of the 'algebraic simplex of size t', {X_0+...+X_n = t}:
(A_n^*) = S{X_0..X_n}/(ΣX_i − t)_{PD} ⊗_S S[dX_0..dX_n]/(ΣdX_i),
where S{..} denotes the divided power polynomial algebra. Eliminating X_n = t − ΣX_α identifies this with S{X_0..X_{n−1}}[dX_0..dX_{n−1}]. In degree n it is free of rank 1 over S{X_0..X_{n−1}}, with basis dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−1}.

Grothendieck defines an S-linear 'integration over the simplex' κ^n : (A_n^*)^n → S. This is the PD analogue of Sullivan/Whitney integration of polynomial forms over Δ^n, which yields a de Rham-type comparison map to cochains. He sets
κ^n(X_0^{(i_0)}···X_{n−1}^{(i_{n−1})} dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−1}) = γ_{i_0..i_{n−1}} · t^{(n+Σi_α)}.
The structure is forced: the real integral over tσ_n is homogeneous of degree n+Σi in t. He wants the coefficient γ to be a 'canonical integer', given by
γ_i = ((n+Σi_α)!/Π i_α!) ∫_{σ_n} X^i dX, with σ_n = {X_α ≥ 0, ΣX_α ≤ 1}.
He checks the normalisation γ_{0..0} = n!·vol(σ_n) = 1, marked with a '?'.

Second method: induction on n via Stokes.
- Write the top form as d(X_{n−1}^{(i_{n−1}+1)} X_0^{(i_0)}···X_{n−2}^{(i_{n−2})} dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−2}).
- On the faces X_α = 0 (α < n−1) the form dies because dX_α restricts to 0. On the face X_{n−1} = 0 it dies because X_{n−1}^{(m)} with m ≥ 1 vanishes there.
- Only the face X_0+...+X_{n−1} = t survives. Substituting X_{n−1} = t − (X_0+...+X_{n−2}) reduces κ^n to κ^{n−1} of (t − ΣX)^{(i_{n−1}+1)} X_0^{(i_0)}···dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−2}.
- Expand with the PD multinomial formula: (t − ΣX)^{(m)} = Σ_{λ+Σl=m} (−1)^{Σl} t^{(λ)} Π X_α^{(l_α)}.
- Multiply using X^{(i)}X^{(l)} = c_{i,l} X^{(i+l)} with c_{i,l} = binom(i+l,i), and t^{(λ)} t^{(N)} = c_{λ,N} t^{(λ+N)}.

This gives the recursion
γ_{i_0..i_{n−1}} = ±Σ_{λ+Σl_α = i_{n−1}+1} (−1)^{Σl_α} Π c_{i_α,l_α} · c_{λ, n−1+Σ(i_α+l_α)} · γ_{i_0+l_0,...,i_{n−2}+l_{n−2}}.
The recursion visibly makes all γ integers, which is the point. It shows κ^n is defined over any PD base, and that integration of PD forms over the simplex needs only the divided powers of t.
errors: Grothendieck treats γ_{i_0..i_{n−1}} as an unknown 'canonical integer' and only checks γ_{0..0} (with a '?'). By the Dirichlet integral ∫_{σ_n} Π X_α^{i_α} dX = Π i_α! / (n+Σi_α)!, in fact γ_i = 1 for every multi-index. Hence κ^n(X^{(i)} dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−1}) = t^{(n+Σi_α)}, and the Stokes recursion collapses to a binomial identity.
The inequality string '0 ≤ ... ≤ (1/n!)γ_{0..0} ?= 1/n!' is a loose estimate. The bound actually holds on the real integral (≤ vol σ_n = 1/n!), not on γ.

Sign bookkeeping in the Stokes step is unclear. The global factor (−1)^{i_{n−1}+1} written in the penultimate line duplicates the (−1)^{Σl} already in the PD expansion, and the orientation sign (−1)^{n−1} of the face is not tracked. Signs must cancel to give γ = 1, so as written the recursion is only correct up to sign.

ideas.what: Simplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham algebra on the simplex ΣX_i = t over a PD base (S, S^+, γ)
ideas.modern_name: PD/integral analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms ∇(n,*); divided-power Sullivan forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); integral/PD variants by Cenkl–Porter and later authors (unsure of exact first appearance)
ideas.where_published: Only the 1976 IHÉS lecture, of which no published text is known to me (unsure)

ideas.what: S-linear integration map κ^n from top PD forms to S, with κ^n(X^{(i)} dX) = t^{(n+|i|)}
ideas.modern_name: fibre integration / Stokes trace for divided-power forms on simplices (integral de Rham comparison map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the rational version is classical (Whitney, Sullivan, Bousfield–Gugenheim)

ideas.what: Computation of the coefficients via the Dirichlet integral and via a Stokes recursion using PD binomial expansion

missed.claim: Grothendieck does not realise (on this page) that all γ equal 1. The clean statement is that the simplex integral on the PD de Rham algebra is κ^n(X^{(i)} dX) = t^{(n+|i|)}, so integration is defined over any PD base once t has divided powers. This gives an integral, PD version of Sullivan's de Rham map A_•^* → C^*(Δ^•) as early as 1976.
missed.quote: où γ_{i_0…i_{n−1}} est un entier canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of homotopy types (binomial rings, PD/cosimplicial models, Toën's and Horel's work, integral Sullivan theory) use exactly such PD/binomial simplicial forms. A documented 1976 Grothendieck construction of the PD simplicial de Rham algebra with an integration map would be an early precursor. Its exact novelty relative to Cenkl–Porter type work is uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck setting up an integral, divided-power version of simplicial polynomial forms with an explicit integration map in 1976. That is historically interesting as a precursor of integral Sullivan-type models. The computation itself is elementary and incomplete (the coefficients are all 1), and similar constructions exist in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Header likely reads 'S, S^+, γ^n, t': base ring, PD ideal, divided powers, element t.
In the κ^n formula the crossed-out prefix is deleted. The exponent of t is (n+Σi_α), with the alternative 'Σ(i_α+1)' written above; they are equal.
Under the Stokes step the form should read d(X_{n−1}^{(i_{n−1}+1)} X_0^{(i_0)}···X_{n−2}^{(i_{n−2})} dX_0∧...∧dX_{n−2}), as in the next line. 'dX_0^{(i_0+1)}' is a misreading or a slip.
The leading factor in 'Donc γ = (...)^{i_{n−1}+1}' is a crossed-out sign, presumably (−1)^{i_{n−1}+1}.
The page number '140' is written at bottom left.
